title: The Captive Who Wrote the Knight
dek: Spanish soldier, captive, playwright, and novelist whose Don Quixote helped invent the modern novel.
mortality_event: Wounded at Lepanto in 1571 and held captive in Algiers for five years before Don Quixote.
citation_passage: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra (1547–1616) was a Spanish soldier and writer best known for Don Quixote. He was seriously wounded at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571. On a later voyage back to Spain, corsairs captured him and his brother and took them to Algiers. Miguel remained captive for five years, attempted escape, and was finally ransomed in 1580. Back in Spain he wrote plays and fiction while also working to support himself. The first part of Don Quixote appeared in 1605. This eight-page biographical comic follows war injury and captivity into the long, uncertain working life that preceded literary success.
